title: Array: swap two cells by dragging one onto the other
description: The core sorting move. With an array selected, drag a cell's value onto another cell to swap them (one undo step); optionally a brief swap animation. Marks travel with values.
acceptance_criteria: Drag cell i onto cell j swaps values (both directions, vertical arrays too); Esc cancels; undo; e2e.
close_reason: Per-cell handles; drag onto another cell swaps values + marks (one undo, Esc cancels), ghost + dashed target while dragging, CSS arc animation on swap. Vertical arrays too. e2e swap.e2e.ts.

title: Mark elements with highlight colours (compare, visited, pivot, sorted)
description: Per-element marks stored on the shape (key -> colour), applied live: hover an element and press 1-4 to toggle a colour (0 clears), or pick from a small palette. Works for array cells, list/tree/graph nodes and edges. Survives edits and re-layout; included in export; one undo per change.
acceptance_criteria: Mark array cells and list nodes in 4 colours via keys and the palette; marks follow nodes through insert/remove/drag; export shows them; e2e.
close_reason: Marks on any element: keys 1-4/0 on the element under the pointer (tldraw numbered toolbar shortcuts disabled), Mark submenu in the context menu, stored per shape (array/list/tree migrations), rendered on canvas and export, pruned on removal, swapped with values. Unit + e2e (marks.e2e.ts, migration).

title: Distinct random values by default, plus a 'repeats allowed' fill mode
description: Random fills in 0..99 repeat often (about 37% chance of a duplicate in 10 values). BSTs need distinct keys and most textbook examples use distinct values. Make random (and letters, up to 26) draw without replacement, including when growing and inserting (skip values already present, typed or not); keep duplicates available as a new 'repeats' fill mode.
close_reason: random/letters draw without replacement (sorted modes strictly monotone) until the pool runs out; extend/insert skip present values; new 'repeats' fill mode keeps duplicates. 8 new unit tests.

title: Hover-revealed node and edge controls
description: A selected list shows ~20 widgets (drag handles, x, +, grips); trees and graphs would be unreadable. Show a node's x only while the pointer is over (or near) that node, and an edge's + only near that edge; grips stay visible. Touch (coarse pointer) shows everything, since there is no hover.
acceptance_criteria: Hover a node -> its x appears; move to the x and click it; + appears near the hovered arrow; nothing per-node shows otherwise; coarse pointer shows all; e2e updated.
close_reason: Node x / edge + appear only near the pointer (hover.ts, 16px reach; grips always shown); coarse pointers show all. Driver 'hover' command + e2e hoverNode helper; list-edit e2e updated and extended.

title: Grow handle: drag to add or remove elements after drawing
description: After an array or list is drawn, select it and drag a '+' grip past its end to add elements (one per cell / node step) or drag back to remove them. Existing (typed) values are kept; new ones follow the shape's fill mode (random continues the seeded stream, ascending/descending continue the run). One undo per drag, Esc cancels. Built on a tldraw 'create' handle (drawn only on hover) plus our own grip glyph, so later structures can reuse it.
acceptance_criteria: Array (both axes) and list (all four directions) grow and shrink via the grip; head stays put on the page for left/up lists; typed values survive; undo/Esc work; unit + e2e tests.
close_reason: Grow grip for arrays (both axes) and lists (4 directions): create-type handle + '+' glyph past the end; grownCount/extendValues pure + unit tests (59 total); e2e grow.e2e.ts (5 tests, x4 stable) incl. typed values kept, seeded continuation, head fixed for left lists, Esc, undo.

title: Node-link render kit: nodes, edges, arrowheads, labels
description: Theme-aware SVG primitives shared by component() and toSvg(): circle and box nodes, straight edges clipped to node boundaries, arrowheads, curved antiparallel edges (u->v and v->u), self-loops, edge labels (weights), null/ground marker, pointer-box arrows for list nodes. Geometry helpers are pure and unit-tested.
acceptance_criteria: Used by at least the list shape; edge clipping/curving covered by vitest; looks right in light and dark export.
close_reason: src/nodelink/geometry.ts + SceneSvg.tsx: circle/box/list nodes, clipped straight edges, curved antiparallel twins, self-loops, arrowheads, edge labels, null/label annotations; pointer arrows take the shortest path. 16 vitest; list rendered in app; circles/curves/loops/labels checked visually via a rendered sample scene (light + dark).

title: Decide node-link representation: one model-driven shape vs tldraw node shapes + bound arrows
description: Lists/trees/graphs could be (a) ONE custom shape per structure whose props hold the model (nodes, edges, per-node position overrides) and render everything in SVG, or (b) separate node shapes joined by tldraw arrows with bindings. This choice shapes every later wave.
design: DECIDED (2026-10-02): option (a), one model-driven shape per structure. Implemented as src/nodelink: subclasses of NodeLinkShapeUtil turn props into a Scene (pure), the base renders (SceneSvg, shared with export), edits values (sceneCells -> CellShapeUtil) and drags nodes via tldraw vertex handles placed on each node's bottom edge (centre handles covered the values). Drag offsets are stored per node (dx/dy) on top of the automatic layout; 'Re-layout' (context menu) clears them. Spike = the singly linked list (dds-55z.8), which became the real first consumer. Open UX question: dragging requires selecting the structure then grabbing the handle; revisit if teachers expect to grab the node body.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded in design notes; a throwaway spike renders a 3-node list and drags one node, confirming the chosen approach in tldraw 5.5.
close_reason: Decided: one model-driven shape per structure; proven by the linked list (render, edit, drag, export, undo).

title: Wave 2: node-link foundations
description: Shared pieces every node-and-pointer structure (lists, trees, heaps, graphs) needs before its own tool: a representation decision, an SVG render kit for nodes and edges, node editing via the cell layer, node dragging, structure options in the style panel, seeded generation, and browser e2e tests.
close_reason: Wave 2 complete: node-link kit, seeded fills, node editing/dragging, style-panel options, e2e harness.

title: Array sketch tool: drag to grow cells with random integers
description: Custom 'array' shape + tool. Press and drag: a new cell appears every cellSize page pixels along the dominant drag axis (right/left/down/up), each filled with a random int. Dragging back shrinks the array (values are kept stable). One undo step per array; Esc cancels. Indices shown under/next to cells. Uses tldraw color style. SVG rendering so export works.
acceptance_criteria: Toolbar button + shortcut (A). Drag right/left/up/down produces a correctly oriented array; release selects it; undo removes it in one step; export to SVG/PNG includes cells, values and indices.
close_reason: Array shape + tool done: drag grows cells every cell-width in any of 4 directions, random ints 0-99, stable values on shrink/regrow, indices, colour/size/font styles, Esc cancel, single-step undo, SVG export. Verified with 13 unit tests and a headless-Chrome drive.

title: Scaffold Vite + React + TS app with tldraw
description: Vite React-TS project, tldraw dependency, full-screen <Tldraw> with persistenceKey, typecheck/build/test scripts, vitest.
acceptance_criteria: npm run dev shows a tldraw canvas; npm run build and npm test pass.
close_reason: Vite 8 + React 19 + TS 7 + tldraw 5.5 scaffold; dev/build/typecheck/test scripts; vitest passing.

title: drawds v1: sketchable data structures on tldraw
description: Teacher-facing whiteboard built on the tldraw SDK (https://tldraw.dev). Each data structure (array, matrix, linked list, stack/queue, tree, graph, map) is a custom tldraw shape plus a gesture-driven tool, so a teacher can sketch a structure in one stroke and get it pre-filled (empty, random, sorted, ...) and editable. Shared pieces: data/fill generators, theme-aware SVG rendering (so export to PNG/SVG for slides works), and UI overrides for the toolbar.
notes: Planning lens (from user testing of lists): for every structure, list the moves a teacher invokes live (insert, delete, extend, swap, mark, point, rotate...) and make them first-class beads in the wave, not afterthoughts. Creation gestures alone are not enough.

title: Clean copy: a structure's copy without marks or pointers, beside it
description: Teachers mark up a structure during a lesson and want the same one again, fresh. One item in every structure's menu puts a copy (same values and shape, same seed) beside the original with no marks or pointers; one undo step; the copy is selected. Followers (graph views, recursion trees) are not copied.
close_reason: Clean copy in every structure's own submenu (src/cells/clean-copy.ts), under the original past anything in the way; unit + e2e.

title: Pinned seed: draw the same values again (style panel Seed field, all structures)
description: Every structure stores a seed and its generator rebuilds the same values from it; sketch tools pick a fresh one at press. Style panel Seed row: pin a seed (typed, or the selected structure's) and every new sketch of any structure uses it until unpinned (localStorage). New random seeds are short (1-9999) so they fit in lecture notes. Exact for arrays, lists, stacks/queues, heaps, matrices, hash tables, union-find (same length); trees and graphs also depend on the gesture.
close_reason: Pinned seed (src/data/seed.ts, src/ui/SeedPicker.tsx): style panel Seed row, createDragTool uses it; short new seeds; unit + e2e.

title: Matrix labels continue their numbering (0x0 -> 0x1, 0x2...; 0x00, 0x04 -> 0x08...)
description: Follow-up to dds-b19. Typing one numbered label (0x0, 1, Q1) makes the rows/columns after it continue the numbering; two in a row set the step (0x00, 0x04 -> 0x08, 0x0C). Hex keeps 0x and zero padding. Continued labels are derived (not stored), so growing continues them; when every header is numbered they number the places, so inserting / deleting a row keeps the sequence instead of moving labels.
close_reason: Done on branch matrix-label-numbering: numbering.ts (pure) continues numbered labels, step from two typed in a row; numbered headers stay positional on insert/delete. Unit + e2e pass.

title: Matrix: editable row and column labels (e.g. 0x0, 0x1 for a memory heap)
description: TAs asked: change the labels at the side of a matrix, e.g. memory addresses 0x0, 0x1 instead of indices 0, 1. Double-click a row index (left) or column index (above) to type a label; empty falls back to the index. Labels move with their rows/columns (insert/delete/transpose), the left margin widens to fit, cells stay put on the page.
close_reason: Done on branch matrix-labels (uncommitted): double-click a row/column index to label it; labels move with rows/cols, clear via Matrix > Back to indices. Unit + e2e (incl. migration) pass.

title: Recursion tracer for plain functions: gcd, factorial, fib, sayHello (lectures 1, 4a)
description: L1 introduces recursion with gcd(60, 24), factorial and sayHello (no base case: the stack grows until it overflows); 4a notes that fib's subproblems overlap. A shape of its own, chosen from the toolbar with a function and arguments: the call stack as an upright stack of frames (arguments, the pending expression like 3 * fact(2)), the call tree beside it, results flowing back down the stack. fib shows repeated subtrees (lit as repeats); sayHello stops at a capacity with 'stack overflow'.
close_reason: recursion-tracer shape (Shift+R): gcd, fact, fib, sum, sayHello (no base case), a sum that never shrinks; type a call into main or pick the Function; Run steps frames onto the stack and off it, values drop into the frame below, the Java code lights its case; overflow at 8 frames with the output strip; fib's recursion tree opens beside it with repeats marked green. Unit (tracer.test.ts) + e2e (e2e/tracer.e2e.ts).

title: Quicksort and merge sort feed the recursion tree: best vs worst case (lectures 4a, 10a)
description: Each call's range and size as a node; work per level beside each level, totalled (n log n vs n(n-1)/2). Quicksort on random vs sorted input gives the balanced tree vs the stick that 10a draws; merge sort gives the log n levels of n work behind T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n.

title: Divide and conquer sum on an array (lecture 1)
description: L1's task-10 tips: a recursive sum, first + sum(rest) (a stick n deep, the bad space complexity) vs halves (log n deep), with a private helper taking the index range. Both as array operations: the range lit per call, partial sums returned as badges, the recursion tree beside it showing the two shapes.
close_reason: Array menu: 'Sum: last value + sum of the rest' (sumByRest, a stick n deep) and 'Sum by halves (divide and conquer)' (sumByHalves, 2n-1 calls, log n deep), shown when every value is a number; counts calls, max depth, additions; each opens its recursion tree beside the array. Unit + e2e (e2e/recursion-tree.e2e.ts).

title: Recursion tree view beside an operation
description: The biggest gap in the slides: L1 'keeping track with a stack' and 'divide and conquer sum', 4a's analysis of merge sort and recursive binary search (Master theorem), 10a's quicksort best / worst case. A separate shape beside the structure (like graph views: created by the operation, linked by id, deleted with it) drawn from the frames: each call a node labelled with its arguments (qs(0, 7), sum(0..3)), drawn as the call opens, its result added when it returns, the current call lit, the call stack being the path from the root to it. Frames carry call open / return events so any recursive operation can feed it (the quicksort and DFS call stack strips already know them). Levels can carry the work per level (n, n, n for merge sort; n, n-1, n-2 for quicksort on sorted input). Laid out from the whole run up front so it holds still, as the union-find view is. Children: the operations that feed it.
notes: 2026-10-07 (branch recursion-tree): the view is built. Frame.calls ({call} / {returns}) -> src/shapes/recursion/calls.ts (callRun, callStates, callTreeLayout) -> recursion-tree shape (stores the run's calls, follows the playing run whose calls match, else shows the whole run with every result; heading counts calls and depth once the run is over). openRecursionTree(editor, structure, frames, title) before playOperation, onCancel takes it back; reused when a tree with the same calls is already there; new runs go to the right. Followers generalised (src/cells/followers.ts: lesson log, step export, bar placement, deletion). First feeder: dds-szw.13.2 (sums). Left: quicksort / merge sort (13.1), recursive binary search (13.3), the tracer (13.4); tree recursion (dds-szw.2) can feed it too.

title: Graph: find a path from A to B; is there a cycle? (lecture 9a)
description: 9a's 'path and cycle' drawing, and 9b's 'DFS detects cycles, BFS finds shortest paths'. (1) Path from a node to another (prompt, or pick the second node): BFS with the queue strip and parent links, then the path lit green, fewest edges; says so when B can't be reached. (2) Is there a cycle?: DFS (undirected: a visited neighbour that isn't the parent; directed: a neighbour still on the stack), the cycle lit when found. Reuse traverse.ts's Recorder.

title: Array scans from lectures 2 and 3: find the max, all unique?, sentinel search
description: Lecture 3 analyses max(A) and unique(A) by counting the basic operation; lecture 2 has sequential search with a sentinel. (1) Find the max: a maxval badge or pointer, i walks, n-1 comparisons. (2) All unique?: i / j nested loop, every pair compared and counted against n(n-1)/2 (all unique is the worst case; a duplicate stops it, both lit red); optionally 'sort, then compare neighbours' for the faster way ('unique more ways'). (3) Linear search with a sentinel: the key goes into a spare cell, the loop runs without the bounds check, the key is taken out again; the counts show the comparisons saved.

title: Shuffles step by step: naive vs Fisher-Yates (lecture 2)
description: Lecture 2 sets the unfair shuffle (for i in 0..n-1, swap a[i] with a[rand(n)]) against Fisher-Yates (for i from n-1 down to 1, swap a[i] with a[rand(i+1)]). Today Shuffle is instant (rearrange.ts). Two operations in a Shuffles group: i and r as pointers, the pick in the caption with its range ('r = random 0..4: 2'), swap arcs as in the sorts, Fisher-Yates' finished suffix faded with dim. Seeded, so a replay is the same run. The two look almost the same on screen, which is the slide's point; the outcome tree shows the difference.

title: Tree recursion that returns values: count leaves, height, size (lecture 8a)
description: 8a draws counting leaves and the height of a tree recursively, asking for the base and recursive cases and 'when do we count?'. Operations from a node (nodeOperations, so a subtree works too) on binary trees, BSTs and heaps: post-order recursion with the call stack as a strip (calls named like height(B)), each node lit as its call opens and badged with its result when it returns (an empty child returns 0 or -1, shown greyed); the caption forms the sum or max ('height(B) = 1 + max(0, 1) = 2'). Predict mode asks 'what does height(B) return?'. Ends on the root's badge. Can feed the recursion tree view.

title: Quicksort with a cut-off to insertion sort
description: Sub-arrays of k or fewer values (k asked for, default 3) finish with insertion sort instead of recursing; the call stack shows the switch and the caption says why (recursion is costly on small arrays, which are already partly in order).

title: Three-way partition (Dutch national flag)
description: lt, i and gt pointers: smaller values go left, larger right, equal ones gather in the middle and are never sorted again. Best shown with the repeats fill; quicksort's recursive calls then skip the equal block.

title: Quicksort with median of three
description: Each call compares a[lo], a[mid], a[hi] (lit together; predict mode asks 'which is the median?'), puts the median at hi, then partitions. Three samples cost O(1); the true median would cost O(n) per call.

title: Quicksort with a random pivot
description: Each call picks a random index in lo..hi (seeded, so a replay is the same run), swaps it to hi, then partitions as Lomuto does; the caption says which was picked and why (a random pick is likely nearer the middle). On sorted input the call stack stays shallow where the last-value pivot goes n deep.

title: Quicksort improvements step by step (lecture 10a)
description: Lecture 10a draws four improvements after Lomuto partition. We have partition (both schemes) and quicksort with its call stack strip and dim, but none of these. Each is its own entry in the sorts group, reusing the recorder in operations.ts, so the counts (comparisons, swaps) compare them with plain quicksort on the same input, sorted input in particular (the worst-case slide). Children: one per improvement.

title: DD1338 coverage: every lecture drawing as a live animation
description: A test for drawds: can it replace the tablet drawings in DD1338 (Algorithms and Data Structures)? First pass over the 17 lecture decks (Google Drive, slide text only, so what each slot showed is inferred from the slides around it): the 14 algorithms and data structures decks have 58 'Draw:' slots. 27 already run live in drawds, 10 partly, 14 need new features, 7 are pen-and-paper maths or analogies best left to freehand (summations, induction proofs, the Arlanda Express). The OOP decks (4b, 5b, 6b) and the IDE code demos are out of scope. Children are the gaps worth having on hand for a live demo: moves on structures we already have, and new capabilities within the vision (recursion trees, cost accounting, shuffle outcomes, tree terms, representation costs). Ruled out as diluting the tool: growth charts / Big-O curves, PageRank, maze grid graphs, expression trees. Second pass: the lecture transcripts, to confirm what was drawn in each slot and rank by teaching time. Lecture 1 is the thinnest and comes first (mid-November, if last year's timetable holds).
notes: Slot by slot (first pass, 2026-10-07). Live: L2 selection / insertion sort; L5a common ADTs, SLL and DLL, list operations; L6a stack operations, array vs linked implementation; L7a collisions, chaining vs probing, table grow; L7b dynamic table (Append 8 values, doubling); L8a pre / in / post-order (+ level order); L8b BST, search, insert, delete cases 1, 2, 3.1, 3.2; L9a graph creation, graph types; L9b memory structures, DFS, BFS, counting components; L10a partition. Partly: L1 keeping track with a stack (strips only inside operations); L3 counting search, insertion sort best / worst (play bar counts, no cost x times table); L7a Bus Map, compression (k mod m only); L8a tree terms; L8b priority list vs tree; L9a adjacency / neighbours / degree (dds-55z.19.8); L10a best / worst case (counts, no recursion tree). Missing: L1 divide and conquer sum, (PageRank, curves of complexity: ruled out); L2 unfair / Fisher-Yates permutations; L7b accounting method; L8a counting leaves, height; L8b min / max; L9a path and cycle; L10a randomise, median of three, three-way partition, cut-off to insertion sort. Pen and paper: L3 summations (3), L4a proof by example / induction (3), L7b Arlanda Express. Demos: L6a hand stack = dds-55z.33; L9a sparse / dense / fully connected (complete missing).

title: Lesson log: every operation played live, exportable afterwards
description: The teacher wants to teach live, then make lecture notes afterwards from the session transcript plus the board. Step export (35.4) only works for the operation still open: once closed, its steps are gone, and re-running it later starts from a board that has moved on. Record each operation as it is played (label, time, the shape before, its frames, the result) in the board (document meta or a page of its own, saved with the .tldr), with a 'Lesson' list to re-open any recorded operation in its bar and export its steps, and a driver/dev hook to export all of them in order (time-stamped, so they line up with a transcript).
acceptance_criteria: Play three operations on different shapes, change the board, then reopen the first from the lesson log and export its steps as they were; the log survives save/open of the board; one command exports every recorded operation in order with timestamps; e2e.
close_reason: Lesson log: playback's recordOperations hook records every live operation (shape + views as they were, frames, result + final highlights, outcome, when each step was shown) into the board's document meta (drawdsLesson, history-ignored, saved with .tldr). Main menu > Lesson log… lists them (time, structure, first step, how far it got): Replay (in place, migrated records, out of undo, board put back on close or after a reload), Save steps, Save all (folders + lesson.json), Clear. Dev window.drawdsLesson + driver 'lesson' (folders, lesson.json with shownAt per step, steps.json per folder for deck.py). Verified: three ops, board changed, replay of the first shows it as it was; undo after a replay undoes the last real change; save/open keeps the log; reload mid-replay restores the board. 373 vitest, 203 e2e x3.

title: Node-link geometry follows the step being shown
description: Arrays size their geometry from displayShape, so a step with more cells stays inside the box. Node-link shapes don't: getGeometry uses the committed scene, so while a step's scene or props change the structure's size (hash rehash to a bigger table, a list node off the line, a heap growing) the selection box keeps the old bounds and drawing can spill outside it (ghosts). Make NodeLinkShapeUtil.getGeometry (and the layout offset used for the step) follow displayScene reactively, keeping the drawing still on the page (as PlaybackView.committed does for commits).
acceptance_criteria: During hash rehash, list insert / delete and heap insert the selection box covers what the step draws; nothing moves on the page when a step changes size; bounds e2e extended to check a step mid-operation; dds-55z.30's playback note resolved.
close_reason: Open operations make room for their steps: NodeLinkShapeUtil.withPlaybackRoom puts the union of every step's extent in meta.drawdsRoom (set on open, cleared around the commit and on close, history-ignored); the layout offset counts it, so onBeforeUpdate moves the shape and nothing shifts on the page, and the geometry gets internal corner points so the box holds every step. Caches keyed by props also key on meta / offset. clearStaleRooms on mount and after undo. bounds e2e: every step of list insert / insert-head / delete, heap insert and hash rehash inside the box with an untouched node still, plus undo.

title: Quality: steps drawn inside the box, steady tests
description: Recurring classes of issue from the 2026-10-04 review: what a step draws can fall outside the shape's box (selection outline, ghosts when the camera moves), and the e2e suite relies on fixed sleeps around closing menus. See also dds-55z.30 and dds-55z.19.10.
close_reason: All four children done: node-link geometry follows the step, menu waits in e2e, the flaky BST test, roots that stay still. Leftovers live in dds-55z.30 and dds-55z.19.10.

title: Consistent menus, and a 'what can I do here?' hint
description: Menus grew one structure at a time: 'Step by step', 'Stack', 'Queue', 'Graph algorithms', 'Show beside it', 'Rows and columns', 'Hash table', 'Matrix'... A teacher has to learn each structure's layout. Settle one shape for every structure's context menu (e.g. Edit / Step by step / Show / Actions, operations named as verbs), rename submenus to match (keeping test ids stable via submenuId), and add a small hint for the selected structure listing its gestures, buttons and shortcuts (a '?' in the style panel or a first-use tooltip).
acceptance_criteria: Every structure's menu follows the documented layout (written up in CLAUDE.md); the hint lists each structure's moves; existing e2e still pass with stable test ids; screenshots of each structure's menu reviewed.
close_reason: One context-menu layout for every structure, enforced in NodeOperationsMenu: Step by step (animated, default section) > a submenu named by menuName (section 'actions': instant changes) > Show (section 'show') > Mark > Pointer, empty ones left out; groups divide families (searches, sorts, traversals); element ops name the element. Submenu test ids follow sections (drawds-<menuId>-steps|actions|show); item ids unchanged; e2e updated. 'What can I do?' in the style panel: a popover of the selected structure's moves (util.moves) plus shared ones. Documented in CLAUDE.md and the run-drawds skill; e2e/menus.e2e.ts locks the layout per structure and tests the hint; menus reviewed from screenshots and a full inventory.

title: Save and open boards as files
description: Boards live only in this browser's IndexedDB (persistenceKey); the tldraw SDK doesn't ship tldraw.com's file menu. Teachers prepare boards before class and want to hand them to students or move them between machines. Add Save board / Open board (and Ctrl+S / Ctrl+O) to the main menu using tldraw's snapshot API (getSnapshot / loadSnapshot) as a .tldr-style JSON file, with our shape migrations applying on load.
acceptance_criteria: Main menu items and shortcuts save a file and open it again in a fresh browser profile with every structure, mark, pointer and style intact; files from older schema versions migrate; e2e saves and reloads a board with one of each structure.
close_reason: Main menu Open board / Save board / Save board as (Ctrl+O / Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S) as .tldr via tldraw's serializer and parser (migrations run on open); File System Access pickers in Chrome (Save writes back to the picked file, keyed by document meta so undoing an Open can't overwrite it), download + file input elsewhere; opening is one undo step with an Undo toast; tab title names the board. e2e/board-files.e2e.ts: every structure round-trips into a fresh profile, older schema migrates, bad file leaves the board alone.

title: Predict, then reveal: let the class guess each step
description: Active learning on top of the step-through engine: a mode (a toggle on the play bar, remembered like autoplay) where each step first shows a question instead of its result: the caption's assignment or comparison hidden behind a '?', the element about to change pulsing. The next press reveals the step (highlights, swaps, new values), the one after moves on. E.g. 'Which slot will 29 land in?' before the probe, 'Which node does BFS discover next?'. Frames may give an optional question (Frame.ask) where the default ('What happens next?') is weak.
acceptance_criteria: Toggle on the bar; in predict mode each step takes two presses (question, then reveal); stepping back undoes reveals cleanly; Space/autoplay still plays straight through; at least BFS, BST insert and hash insert have tailored questions; e2e for the two-press rhythm.
close_reason: Predict mode: a ? toggle on the play bar (remembered, drawds:predict). Stepping by hand, each step is first a question (Frame.ask, default 'What happens next?') over the step before, with askFocus elements pulsing violet (SceneSvg pulse); the next press reveals; back undoes one press at a time (pure stepFrom / shownFrame, unit-tested); Space / autoplay play straight through; nothing is asked once the result is in. Tailored, answer-neutral questions in BFS, DFS, BST insert and search, hash insert / find / delete. e2e/predict.e2e.ts.

title: Step operations with a presentation clicker (PageDown / PageUp)
description: Presentation clickers send PageDown / PageUp (some send arrow keys or B for blank). While an operation's bar is open, PageDown should step forward and PageUp step back, captured on the window like the play bar's other keys (Space, Left / Right, Enter, Esc), so a teacher can walk around the room while stepping through Dijkstra. Swallow their keyup as the other bar keys do (drawds-gotchas 7).
acceptance_criteria: With a bar open, PageDown steps forward (commits at the end like Right), PageUp steps back; tldraw's own PageUp/Down handling doesn't also fire; e2e covers both; the bar's key hint / tooltips mention them.
close_reason: PageDown/PageUp step the play bar like Right/Left (repeat while held, Shift+PageDown keeps highlights at the end), captured ahead of tldraw; tooltips name them; e2e in playback.e2e.ts

title: On-canvas push / pop and enqueue / dequeue buttons
description: While a stack or queue is the only selected shape: + push above the top and x pop on the top cell; + enqueue at the rear slot and x dequeue on the front cell. They play the operations (next value from the fill mode), like the BST insert button.

They play the operations with the fill mode's next value.

title: Queue enqueue / dequeue / peek step by step (circular buffer, wrap-around)
description: Fixed (circular buffer): enqueue a[rear] = v; rear = (rear + 1) % capacity, narrated when it wraps to 0; size++ (full: size = capacity, nothing changes); dequeue v = a[front]; blank; front = (front + 1) % capacity; size-- (empty: underflow). Growing (a list): enqueue appends; dequeue takes a[0] and shifts every value left, one copy each: why circular buffers. Front / rear markers slide.
close_reason: Queue submenu: Enqueue / Enqueue a value... / Dequeue / Peek. Circular buffer: a[rear] = v then rear = (rear + 1) % capacity, narrated when it wraps; full when size = capacity; dequeue frees a[front], front moves on, nothing else moves. Growing (a list): enqueue appends; dequeue shifts every value left (moves counted) and says why circular buffers. Grow copies a circular buffer in queue order so its front lands at 0.

title: Stack push / pop / peek step by step (overflow, underflow)
description: Push: top = top + 1; a[top] = v (fixed and full: 'stack overflow', nothing changes; growing: a new cell on top). Pop: v = a[top]; the slot goes blank; top = top - 1 (empty: 'stack underflow'). Peek: light a[top]. top marker slides; value prompts or the fill mode's next value.
close_reason: Stack submenu: Push (fill mode's next value), Push a value... (prompt at the top cell via NodeOperation.promptAt), Pop (value to a 'popped' strip, slot blank, top drops), Peek. Fixed and full: stack overflow, nothing changes; empty: underflow; growing: a new cell on top / the cell goes. Capacity > Grow for fixed stacks (and queues). src/shapes/array/stack-queue.ts + tests.

title: Array kind: stack (upright, top marker) and queue (front / rear, circular buffer)
description: Kind picker array / stack / queue in the style panel (StyleProp drawds:array-kind, props kind + front, migration). Stack: drawn upright, index 0 at the bottom (layout axis 'up': cell order, cellAt, hovered cell, grow grip, boundaries, spare slots, second row), built-in top marker at size - 1 (-1 when empty). Queue: a row; built-in front / rear markers (rear = next free slot); fixed capacity = circular buffer (values in front .. front + size - 1 mod capacity, the others blank), growing = a list. Built-in markers are drawn with the pointers and count in the bounds, but can't be picked up or renamed.
close_reason: Kind picker array / stack / queue (StyleProp drawds:array-kind; props kind + front; migration with unit + e2e load check). Stacks stand upright (layout axis 'up' in the metrics: index 0 at the bottom at the origin, which rises as cells come so index 0 stays put; boundaries, indices, grip, sketching up from the press point) with a built-in top marker. Queues lie in a row with front / rear markers; fixed = circular buffer (spare slots per cell, may wrap; unwrapped when it becomes something else or its capacity changes). Built-in markers: CellShapeUtil.markerPointers, laid out with the pointers, not interactive (ids '@...'). Plain arrays keep swap handles and quick x / +.

title: Play bar holds still: anchored bottom-left, buttons first, one position per operation
description: The bar was centred under the structure, so its width (the caption) moved every button left and right, and it moved up and down as strips or a second row came and went: hard to hit pause mid-animation (reported by the user 2026-10-03). Anchor its left edge to the structure's left edge; put every button in a fixed group first (back, play, forward, step counter, speed, autoplay, done/cancel), then the counts chip, then the caption, the only part that grows. Place the bar (and strips) once per operation, under the lowest point any of its steps reaches.
close_reason: Bar anchored at the structure's left edge, buttons first in fixed places (fixed-width step counter), counts then caption last; the bar is top-aligned so a wrapping caption grows downwards. Strips and bar placed once per operation from every step's extent (playbackLayout(shape, frame) -> left/bottom; view.frames), so they never move while it plays. e2e checks button positions across a sort and a grow.

title: Grow a fixed array: new array of twice the capacity, copy, replace (second row of cells)
description: newArr = new int[2 * capacity] appears as a second row under the array (aligned cells, title, indices); each a[i] arcs down into newArr[i] (copies counted); then a = newArr: the row moves up into place and the old array is gone. Needs frames that can show a second row (props.aux) with slides between the rows; geometry grows downward only. Reusable later for merge sort's run and counting sort.
close_reason: Capacity > Grow: double the capacity. Frames gained a second row (props.aux: newArr = new int[2c], aligned cells, title, indices) under a horizontal array (right of a vertical one); values arc down a[i] -> newArr[i] one step each (copies counted), then a = newArr moves them up into the longer array. Geometry and the play bar include the row; moves keyed aux:<i>; crossSlides in swap.ts.

title: Append n values: doubling vs growing by one (amortised O(1))
description: Append a run of values to a fixed array, growing when full, with the growth policy chosen: double, or one more cell. Each grow copies everything at once (one step), the play bar counts appends and copies; the last step compares: doubling stays under 2 copies per append, +1 grows with n.
close_reason: Capacity > Append 8 values, doubling / growing by one when full: each grow is newArr + copy-all + replace in three steps, appends and copies counted (from a full 4: doubling 12 copies for 8 appends, +1 60 copies), the last step names amortised O(1) vs O(n) per append.

title: Fixed arrays: insert, delete and append step by step (full array stops)
description: Insert at k: if size < capacity shift a[size-1..k] right one at a time, a[k] = v, size++; if full, a single step says so (nothing changes) and points at Grow. Delete a[k]: shift left, clear the last used slot, size--. Append: a[size] = v; size++ (O(1), no shifting); grows first when full (see the growth bead).
close_reason: Fixed mode: Insert / delete step by step (insert shifts into the spare slot then size++, full array stops with one step pointing at Grow; delete shifts left, last used slot blank, size--) and Capacity > Append a value (a[size] = v, size++; grows to twice the capacity first when full). Unit + e2e.

title: Array Length option: grows / fixed; size, spare slots, size and capacity shown
description: StyleProp drawds:array-sizing (grows | fixed) in the style panel, props sizing + size (migration). Fixed: cells past size are blank spare slots (not editable or markable), a heavier line at the size boundary, 'size 5 · capacity 8' under the indices; the grow grip adds or removes spare capacity (never below size); sketching fills every cell; switching to fixed keeps every value used, back to grows drops the spare slots. Every operation (search, sort, instant actions, refill, hover x / +) works on the used part only; + only while there is room.
close_reason: Length picker (grows / fixed) in the style panel; props sizing + used (migration, unit + e2e load check). Fixed: blank spare slots behind a heavier size line, 'size · capacity' under the indices, grip changes capacity (never below size), spare slots not editable / markable / draggable, operations and instant actions work on the used part, hover x keeps capacity, + only while there is room. Switching back to grows drops the spare slots (one undo).

title: Fixed-capacity arrays (C / Java arrays): size vs capacity, and growing them
description: Arrays have so far behaved like Python lists (the grow grip, insert's n = n + 1 and delete just change the length), hiding the cost C and Java students need to see. Add a per-array Length option: grows (default, today's behaviour) or fixed capacity, where cells are the capacity and a size counts the used prefix; spare slots are blank. That opens up the dynamic-array growth algorithm behind ArrayList, std::vector and Python lists.
design: Decisions (user, 2026-10-03): growing stays the default; spare slots are always blank; in fixed mode inserting into a full array stops (Grow is a separate step) and only Append grows automatically, like ArrayList.add.
close_reason: All four children done: Length option (grows / fixed, size and spare slots), fixed insert / delete / append step by step, Grow with a second row, append-many doubling vs +1.

title: Stacks and queues
description: Stacks and queues are among the most-taught structures and drawds couldn't draw them (BFS / DFS only show them as strips). Make them a kind of array (like BST is a kind of tree), so they get pointers, marks, the play bar, fixed capacity and growing for free: a stack drawn upright, index 0 at the bottom, with a top marker; a queue as a row with front and rear markers, a circular buffer when its capacity is fixed. Teacher moves: push / pop / peek, enqueue / dequeue / peek, step by step and from on-canvas buttons; overflow and underflow; the wrap-around (rear = (rear + 1) % capacity) and the full-vs-empty question; why a growing list makes a poor queue (dequeue shifts everything).

Stack: vertical, bottom-up (layout axis 'up'), built-in top marker at size - 1 (-1 when empty, on a dashed slot). Queue: horizontal; front / rear markers (rear = next free slot); fixed capacity = circular buffer, values in front .. front + size - 1 mod capacity, the rest blank; growing = a list, front always 0. Built-in markers are drawn like pointers but can't be picked up. (2) Stack operations: push (top = top + 1; a[top] = v), pop (v = a[top]; a[top] blank; top = top - 1), peek; fixed and full: stack overflow; empty: underflow; growing: push appends, pop drops the last cell. (3) Queue operations: enqueue (a[rear] = v; rear = (rear + 1) % capacity; size++), dequeue (v = a[front]; blank; front = (front + 1) % capacity; size--), peek; wrap-around narrated; full / empty via size; growing: dequeue shifts every value left (O(n): why circular buffers). (4) On-canvas buttons: push / pop on the stack, enqueue / dequeue on the queue, playing the operations. Later: circular buffer drawn as a ring; linked stack / queue (needs the list tail pointer, dds-55z.16.1); stack demos (balanced brackets, postfix evaluation).

design:
Investigation 2026-10-06 (spike in the running app, no code kept):
- Mechanism (verified): a store side effect, editor.sideEffects.registerBeforeCreateHandler / registerBeforeChangeHandler('shape'), returns the next record with the transcript in its meta. It runs inside the same store change, so the line joins the move's undo step: redo restored it, board files (.tldr) and IndexedDB keep it, no props migration needed.
- Undo / redo: tldraw has no public 'undo in progress' flag (HistoryManager pauses privately), and undo replays go through the handler as source 'user'. Rule that works: a change that brings its own log (prev.meta log !== next.meta log: undo, redo, a loaded board) passes through untouched; a user's edit never touches the log. Verified: undo pops the line, redo brings it back.
- Coalescing (verified): typing in one cell rewrites its own last line (a[0] = 4 -> a[0] = 42); a creating gesture (editor.isIn('<type>.sketching')) rewrites one creating line; creation via registerBeforeCreateHandler.
- Diffs are ambiguous: a committed bubble sort and the instant Sort both diff as a.sort(); heap pushes diff after the sift. So our own operations must say what they did: playOperation's commit and rearrange can set a transient intent (label + parameters) read by the handler; the props diff is the fallback for direct edits (set, append, insert, delete, swap, sorted, reversed; else a '# n values moved' comment).
- Store moves, not text: language-neutral entries ({op: 'set', i, v}, {op: 'call', name: 'bubble_sort'}) in meta.drawdsCode, rendered per language, so switching language re-renders the whole transcript. Ignore layout-only and style changes (dx/dy, positions, direction, size).
- Showing it: a code-view shape bound to its structure, like graph-view (structureId; redrawn from it; deleted with it, src/shapes/graph-view), offered from Show > 'Code beside it'. tldraw_mono font, SVG text (exports match), sized with editor.textMeasure. Algorithm lines sync through playbackFor(structure).frame.line, as graph views follow their graph's highlights.
- Mode and language: document meta (drawdsCode: on, language), main menu toggle plus a picker. Logging can run always (entries are small) and show when asked.
- Caveats: the handler runs on every shape change (drags), so it must early-out cheaply; logs grow (compact into a snapshot line); one transcript per structure, a board script would interleave by a global counter; collaboration n/a.

title: Ghost rendering artefacts after pan/zoom on complex drawings
description: Reported 2026-10-02: on busier drawings, after moving and zooming, stale 'ghost' pixels stay on the canvas until something repaints the area (dragging an image over clears them). Not tldraw load (one shape per structure). Likely Chrome paint invalidation missing content we draw outside a shape's geometry bounds: stroke overhang (marked nodes/cells 1.6x), edge-weight pills and BFS/DFS badges near the bounds, the play bar and queue/stack strip, x / + buttons and grow grips, swap-arc animations; CSS fade/slide animations make it likelier. Outside-bounds content can also vanish when tldraw culls a shape at the viewport edge.
design: Fix first: keep every shape's drawing starting at its origin. After edits that change the bounds (remove, add or move a node, connect to empty space, the + grip), shift node positions so the bounds' min corner is (0, 0) and move the shape's x/y by the same amount (rotated), so nothing moves on the page; trees and lists need the same for drag offsets. Do it on drag end rather than mid-drag, so tldraw's handle maths isn't disturbed. Then the earlier items: pad geometry by stroke width and include edge labels and badges; move transient controls (play bar, strip, buttons, grips) into a tldraw overlay layer. Regression check: after deleting the leftmost node, bounds.minX should be 0 and the .tl-shape box should match the drawn extent.
notes:
Related performance item to check in the same QA pass: a selected node-link shape re-renders and re-routes every edge on each pointer move (hover controls read the pointer in component()); memoise routeScene per scene and measure on a 40-node graph.
2026-10-02 screenshot (user's Desktop, 'Screenshot 2026-10-02 at 17.50.45.png'): a directed graph in dark mode; zooming out left copies of the rightmost node's label (12), left behind in stages and bigger the further back, the text only, not the circle. Cause confirmed in the app: tldraw sizes a shape's box from its geometry bounds' width/height but places it at the shape's origin, assuming bounds start at (0, 0). Delete a graph's leftmost nodes and the drawing starts 110 px in (bounds minX 110, width 158): on screen the drawing spans x 386-545 while tldraw's box spans 276-435, so the rightmost node lies outside the box and isn't repainted properly when the camera moves. The same can happen whenever nodes end up left of or above the origin (dragged nodes in graphs, trees and lists, adding a node via the connect or + grips).
close_reason: Fixed in 3b912a5: drawings now start at the shape's origin (layout offset + compensation), so tldraw's box covers them; e2e/bounds.e2e.ts guards it. Leftovers in dds-55z.30.

close_reason: Delete any node via an x badge per node (HTML RemoveButton; predecessor rewires, list closes the gap, head removal promotes next node in place); insert/remove at head via a start grip and at tail via the end grip; anchorShift keeps surviving nodes fixed on the page. Pure ops + 11 unit tests, e2e list-edit (5 tests x3). Middle insertion split to dds-55z.16.4.

title: Map / hash table tool
description: Bucket array with key->value chains (separate chaining) or open addressing; random key/value fill.
close_reason: Hash table (Shift+B): chaining or linear probing (switching re-inserts), hash worked out in captions (k mod m / char codes), insert / find / delete (tombstones) / grow-and-rehash step by step, load factor, misplaced keys ringed; key:value entries

title: Teaching overlays: index pointers, cell highlights
description: Labelled pointers (i, j, lo, hi) that snap to cells, and per-cell highlight colours, for walking through algorithms.

title: Listen to the algorithms: tones per step, a sweep at the end
description: After the 'sorting algorithms, visualised and audibilised' videos (Timo Bingmann's 15 sorting algorithms in 6 minutes). Each step shown plays a short tone for each element it lights or swaps, pitched by its value at that step: scaled between the structure's smallest and largest values, snapped to a pentatonic scale; letters by alphabetical order. A sort's last step (everything green) plays a quick rising sweep through the sorted array, as the videos do. Works for every structure because it reads only the play bar's view (the step, what is lit, swaps, moves) and the element values via the shape's cells; nothing in the operations changes.
design: src/sound/: a pure mapping (frame + values -> notes), unit-tested; a player on the Web Audio API (an oscillator with a short envelope, no sound files). A react() on currentPlayback (App onMount) fires on each new step (view.id), skipping fading views and steps re-shown when stepping back. Toggle: a secret key while the play bar is open (M for music), stored in localStorage, a small speaker on the bar while on; the keypress is also the user gesture browsers need before playing audio. Expect a short tune, not the videos' whoosh: drawds steps are one comparison or swap on 8-20 values; a hidden 8x / 16x speed would bring it closer.
acceptance_criteria: Off by default and invisible until toggled; unit tests for the value -> note mapping; e2e with AudioContext stubbed: a bubble sort plays the compared values' notes and the closing sweep; no audio work at all while off.

title: Easter eggs: playful extras, off by default
description: Nice to have, not essential: one of the later epics. Playful extras a teacher can find and show off, hidden from the menus and off by default, never in the way of teaching. Each must stay out of the core (watch the playback state, don't change it) and cost nothing when off.

title: Step decks straight into Google Slides
description: dds-55z.35.4 exports steps as images and .claude/skills/run-drawds/deck.py builds a 16:9 .pptx that Google Slides imports. Uploading from an agent session failed on size: the Drive connector's create_file carries the whole file inside the tool call (a 24-slide deck is ~3 MB), and there is no Slides editor connector; Slides createImage needs image URLs Google can fetch. Options: a Slides editor connector plus images hosted where Google can reach them (Drive files shared by link), a small Apps Script that builds the deck from a Drive folder of step images, or the Slides API with the teacher's OAuth from a CLI.

title: Union-find: drag one element onto another to union them
description: The live teaching move for union is a gesture, not a menu and a prompt: drag from an element (a grip like the graph's connect grip) and drop on another to play union(a, b) step by step. Also consider: Same set? (connected) as its own operation, and animating nodes between layouts when trees merge or compress (they jump now).
acceptance_criteria: Dragging an element's grip onto another plays union(a, b); dropping on empty space or itself does nothing; one undo step; e2e.

title: Open a board by dropping its .tldr file on the canvas
description: Board files open from the main menu or Ctrl+O (dds-55z.35.3). Dropping a .tldr file onto the canvas should open it too (register a 'files' external content handler that hands .tldr files to openBoardFile in src/files/board.ts and passes others to tldraw's default).

title: Counting sort step by step
description: Left from dds-55z.20.8.5: a counts array (strip or second row of cells) filled by one pass, prefix sums, then values placed (stable, right to left). Only for small integer ranges; fall back with a caption otherwise.

title: Array algorithms step by step (umbrella)
description: Arrays were the first structure but have had no step-through work, and sorting/searching is the most-taught step-through material. Everything needed exists: named pointers (i, j, lo, mid, hi) that slide, swap arcs, marks, the play bar (opens paused, narration, strips). Children: binary search, simple sorts, partition. Later: merge sort (needs auxiliary arrays), counting sort.
